features.name: Recording Health Monitoring
features.description: Supervise every active recording with low-overhead video-frame, mux/file-growth, process, and finalization evidence so QueueBack detects a live-but-stalled or failed recorder within a bounded time, preserves later footage after recovery, and keeps a truthful actionable state in the tray and filesystem library instead of treating process liveness or parseable metadata as success.
evidence: 2026-08-12 repository inspection established that the release-era recorder proves startup mainly by child survival and does not yet provide comprehensive stalled-frame/output supervision.

2026-08-12 product correction: an attempted broad health-state implementation made a valid completed Practice Tool recording appear Unknown/non-playable and distracted from the requested capture-performance work. The recorder supervisor, recording-state authority, strict app classification, status UI, and associated tests were rolled back to the pre-feature behavior; recorder tests returned to 31+1 and app tests to 30 passing. This feature is therefore not implemented or complete.

2026-08-12 dependency decision: QB-PERF-002 no longer depends on this feature. Performance work may add only the minimal first-frame/progress evidence needed to prove its new capture graph, without reintroducing recording-state/library policy.
acceptance_criteria: A documented backend-neutral recording-health model distinguishes `starting`, internally `suspect`, `recording/healthy`, `recording/stalled`, `recording/recovered-after-incident`, `finalizing`, `finalized`, `finalized-degraded`, `failed-partial`, and `failed-no-output`; current health and the latched session verdict are separate so resumed progress preserves later footage without erasing a known gap.

Every production ffmpeg recording uses `-progress pipe:1`, `-stats_period 1`, and `-nostats`; stdout progress and stderr diagnostics are drained concurrently without blocking, unknown progress keys are forward-compatible, bounded parser state cannot grow per frame, and loss/malformed output cannot leave the session silently healthy forever.

Startup is not announced as healthy merely because ffmpeg is alive: within 15 seconds it must observe an advancing encoded-video `frame` counter and a positive durable `video.mp4` size, or it stops the failed startup attempt, preserves any partial bytes, persists a stable failure reason, and surfaces an actionable error.

During recording, encoded-video frame advancement and actual output-file byte growth are independent required signals; advancing audio timestamps/bytes alone cannot hide a video-frame stall, and frame advancement without durable file growth cannot hide a mux/storage stall. Output time remains diagnostic rather than sufficient health proof.

A required signal silent for five continuous seconds enters a non-user-facing suspect state; silence reaching exactly 15 seconds is a confirmed incident no later than the next one-second observation. Progress before 15 seconds returns to healthy without an incident, while progress after a confirmed incident becomes recovered-after-incident and leaves the session verdict degraded.

Any session whose required frame and file-growth signals each advance at least once in every interval shorter than 15 seconds, with valid process/observer state, cannot transition to a user-visible unhealthy state. A detected recorder scheduling/suspend gap rearms one bounded confirmation window and increments an observer-gap diagnostic instead of immediately blaming ffmpeg.

Unexpected child exit regardless of exit code, nonzero exit, stop timeout/forced kill, progress-channel closure while the child is live, counter regression, output truncation/replacement, confirmed output disappearance, repeated process-inspection failure, and terminal progress-protocol failure map to stable machine reason codes and cannot be finalized as clean success.

A confirmed stall does not automatically kill or endlessly restart a still-live ffmpeg child: QueueBack continues bounded observation so later footage can be preserved, emits transition-only warnings, and records aggregate incident count/duration/longest-stall data. Repair/remux, automatic live restart, and destructive mutation remain outside this feature.

The health reducer accepts declared required/optional signal capabilities rather than GDI, GPU vendor, or encoder names. The current backend requires encoded-frame plus output-byte progress; QB-PERF-002 can add source-frame, queue, device, and surface signals to the same model without creating a second health state machine.

Each new bundle receives an atomically written versioned `recording-state.json` before capture startup. It is the sole durable authority for recording lifecycle, current health, latched verdict, stable reason, bounded incident aggregates, last proven progress, observer gaps, and finalization result; no per-second/per-frame state-file rewrite, root status database, or duplicate health authority is introduced.

Finalization ordering is crash-conservative: persist finalizing; stop poller and ffmpeg; evaluate the structured child/progress/output result; fsync graceful clean/degraded metadata under a noncanonical pending name; atomically publish canonical `metadata.json`; then atomically persist terminal state. A metadata or terminal-state failure leaves the lifecycle authority non-success and never a clean finalized claim; the app additionally requires coherent terminal state plus canonical metadata, so forced kill, unknown exit, or unhealthy video can never be classified as clean success.

Recorder service events carry structured lifecycle/health snapshots with bundle identity and stable reason codes. Tray/headless projections show starting, recording, recovered/stalled, finalizing, and failure states; a failure or degraded terminal result is not immediately overwritten by Idle, while a later explicit new recording may replace the live tray display without erasing the prior bundle state.

The Tauri library reads the versioned state contract conservatively: a valid legacy metadata-only bundle retains its existing behavior; active/finalizing, failed, corrupt-state, and unknown-schema bundles are visibly non-complete, protected from auto-delete and active deletion, and not playback-eligible; a gracefully finalized degraded bundle is playback-eligible only under existing metadata checks and carries a clear interruption warning.

Library summaries and UI expose a typed recording status, stable problem message, physical video availability, and playback eligibility instead of calling every partial item a recovered bundle. Safe game identifiers accept the recorder's existing `digits` or `digits-suffix` collision format while continuing to reject traversal and malformed identifiers, so health state remains discoverable for every recorder-created bundle.

Live Client polling/calibration remains independent descriptive-data health: its failure never refreshes video progress, creates a video stall, or turns stalled video healthy. No active-path ffprobe, full decode, content hashing, full-file read/remux, or high-frequency frontend polling is added.

Deterministic unit and fake-child tests cover progress parsing; exact 5/15-second boundaries; startup; short-pause recovery; repeated/latched incidents; separate frame/file stalls; audio-only advancement; observer gaps; malformed/closed progress; counter/file regression; unexpected zero/nonzero exit; output missing/empty; process inspection errors; graceful stop; ignored `q`/forced kill; shutdown races; poller independence; sticky event ordering; atomic state transitions; and legacy/current/future-unknown app classification using only temporary libraries.

A real-ffmpeg changing `testsrc2` plus audio fixture proves normal startup/progress/finalization and safe forced interruption, while a 30-minute run produces zero false unhealthy transitions, bounded monitor memory/state, advancing frame and output evidence, and a truthful terminal bundle in a sentinel-marked temporary library.

A representative 25-minute-or-longer League recording verifies healthy tray state, no false alert during normal focus/Alt-Tab behavior, truthful normal finalization, app-compatible library classification, and no regression to automatic match lifecycle or Live Client synchronization. Forced interruption behavior is proved by deterministic Windows exit-probe/service tests and the real-FFmpeg forced-interruption fixture rather than a second manual League session.

Applicable recorder, Tauri, frontend, feature-list, and project-wide verification passes; recorder lifecycle/media-library architecture, operator health-state behavior, thresholds, reason codes, and explicit boundaries with QB-CAP-003, QB-CAP-004, QB-CAP-005, QB-DIST-001, and QB-PERF-002 are durably documented with concrete evidence before completion.

features.name: Capture Benchmark and Performance Budget
features.description: Define and automate/reproduce the benchmark used to measure Chronobreak capture overhead and the budget required before performance claims can be made.
evidence: 2026-08-12 completion claim: the guided collector/finalizer, deterministic analyzer, durable benchmark protocol, sanitized reporting, operator preflight, all eight target NVENC runs, media/resource finalization, automated/project checks, canonical state validation, and diff hygiene completed.

The accepted matrix remains formally INVALID because of focus contamination and telemetry gaps. By explicit product decision it is sufficient diagnostic pre-change characterization only; it establishes no negligible-impact or AMD/Intel claim and does not waive QB-PERF-002's valid post-change gates. Detailed results and artifacts are retained in the execution record.
acceptance_criteria: A durable protocol specifies League Practice Tool on Summoner's Rift with default-skin Garen, a fixed mid-lane camera, no measurement input, a preserved/fingerprinted 1920x1080 borderless VSync-off configuration, a 60-second warmup, and a 180-second measurement.

The complete matrix interleaves three 144-FPS baseline/capture pairs and includes one additional uncapped diagnostic baseline/capture pair, using only a sentinel-marked dedicated benchmark recording library.

The guided collector records versioned manifests plus PresentMon frame data, normalized and raw process CPU, system/process RAM, whole-adapter and where-available per-process 3D/Video Encode activity, adapter/process GPU memory, process I/O, output growth, recorder/poller/error diagnostics, concrete capture metadata, and media-validation artifacts without launching, terminating, or reconfiguring League.

The deterministic analyzer retains every run, aggregates capped conditions by the median of three, reports variability and all required frame/resource metrics, emits sanitized JSON and Markdown without absolute user paths, and labels results pass, fail, invalid, or diagnostic.

The capped frame budget is average-FPS loss <=2%, 1%-low FPS loss <=5%, p95 frametime increase <=5%, p99 frametime increase <=8%, and additional dropped frames <=0.1 percentage point; CPU >=90% and GPU 3D >=95% sample-proportion increases must each be <=5 percentage points, with Video Encode separate.

Malformed, short, wrong-process/wrong-cap, counter-incomplete, fingerprint-inconsistent, media-invalid, or excessively variable datasets are invalid; output stalls, encoder or poller lifecycle/final-flush errors, process disappearance, or sustained recorder/ffmpeg memory growth fail resource safety when the dataset is otherwise valid.

Automated fixtures cover calculations, CPU normalization, GPU-engine aggregation, saturation duration, exact gate and variability boundaries, missing/malformed/short data, resource-safety failures, sanitization/determinism, and uncapped diagnostic semantics.

A finalized report from the current Ryzen 5 5600X, RTX 4060, 1920x1080 NVENC configuration retains the completed capped and uncapped matrix, truthfully labels the focus/telemetry-contaminated dataset invalid, confirms every capture passes ffprobe and full decode, and records the product owner's explicit acceptance of this diagnostic evidence instead of a clean pre-change rerun; AMF and QSV are explicitly listed as unvalidated.

If any valid gate fails or an explicitly accepted diagnostic matrix exposes a substantial performance/resource bottleneck, a concrete planned child under EPIC-CAP-PERF is added and linked before this feature is completed; every substantial non-gating diagnostic finding receives a canonical disposition and any required targeted child; capture tuning is not performed within QB-PERF-001.

features.name: Low-Overhead Native Windows Capture
features.description: Replace the recorder's synchronous Windows `gdigrab` system-memory capture, pixel conversion, and GPU upload with one asynchronous exact-HWND WGC/D3D11/direct-NVENC H.264 High 1920x1080 60-FPS production path that meets the League frame-pacing, resource, lifecycle, media-integrity, and truthful-support contract.
evidence: 2026-09-01 architecture disposition: Windows production recording now has one supported path, the in-process exact-HWND WGC/D3D11/NVENC H.264 High 1080p60 recorder. The unvalidated FFmpeg-driven WGC NVENC/AMF/QSV alternative and its selector were retired; FFmpeg remains the audio/mux/probe/export runtime.

Local non-League evidence passed packaged-runtime/release checks, recorder/app/runtime/benchmark/frontend automation, a native source probe, historical matched 240-second backend A/B, native steady/resize/minimize/occlusion/target-close/NVENC-failure fixtures, and the product-owner-accepted 1,800-second native arm with its lost formal resource-series/full-file-decode limitation preserved.

QB-PERF-002 is blocked on the unavailable required Ryzen 5 5600X/RTX 4060 interactive League capped/uncapped matrix. Native AMD/Intel encoder adapters are not implemented and are explicitly unsupported; no negligible-impact or vendor-wide completion claim is justified. Detailed commands, artifacts, decisions, and next action are in the execution record.
acceptance_criteria: A durable design documents the selected Windows capture API and frame path from League's borderless window through pixel-format handling and native hardware encoding, including ownership, synchronization, adapter selection, supported Windows versions, occlusion/minimize/focus behavior, and why rejected alternatives do not meet performance, reliability, packaging, truthful-support, or anti-cheat-safety requirements.

The automatic optimized Windows path uses Windows Graphics Capture against League's exact HWND on Windows 10 version 1903 or later, accepts the operating-system capture indicator when suppression is unavailable, and never depends on restricted border-removal permission, Desktop Duplication whole-output capture, primary-display retry, game injection, or GDI fallback to report optimized success.

Windows frame acquisition and the core capture-buffer model use vendor-neutral Windows graphics interfaces and types, while the implemented encoder boundary is direct native NVENC. Core capture lifecycle, buffering, frame timing, and diagnostics do not branch on marketing GPU names or the developer's RTX 4060; unimplemented AMD/Intel encoders fail as unsupported rather than selecting a parallel capture path.

On every encoder combination declared implemented, steady-state video acquisition and encoder submission keep full frames GPU-resident without a per-frame full-surface GPU-to-system-memory readback or CPU pixel conversion. Where zero-copy sharing is impossible, any GPU-to-GPU copy or conversion is explicit, bounded, measured, and backend-specific; inspection, diagnostics, or trace evidence proves the actual runtime path rather than inferring it solely from the configured encoder name.

The production runtime is an audited, exactly compatible packaged FFmpeg build initially pinned to 8.1.2 for audio, muxing, probing, and export; startup verifies its version/build identity and FFmpeg/ffprobe pairing. Native capture and encoder initialization independently verify the selected D3D11 adapter, required interop, encoder availability, and diagnostics contract. An arbitrary PATH binary, including the current FFmpeg 6.1, cannot be accepted or trigger a silent legacy fallback.

Native encoder selection is capability-driven and binds capture plus encoding to the correct physical adapter. NVIDIA/NVENC is the current implemented combination. AMD/AMF and Intel/QSV remain unsupported until native encoder adapters are implemented and validated; multiple adapters, unsupported interop, encoder absence, and unimplemented vendors produce deterministic explicit unsupported states without a hidden external-capture or host-copy path.

Frame acquisition and encoding are asynchronous with respect to League and use explicitly bounded queues/resources. When capture or encoding falls behind, the recorder applies a documented recorder-frame drop/backpressure policy, exposes dropped/backlogged capture diagnostics, and cannot grow memory without bound or synchronously stall the game-facing graphics path.

Machine-readable diagnostics separately expose source frames surfaced, source frames superseded by the bounded latest-frame policy, CFR discards, CFR duplications, encoded frames, pool/size recreations, current bounded depth, first/latest Windows Graphics Capture QPC timestamps, progress, and terminal errors; counters are monotonic, their owned-flow accounting invariant is tested, and compositor frames never surfaced by Windows are explicitly outside the claim.

Recording and Live Client timestamps are anchored to the first Windows Graphics Capture SystemRelativeTime/QPC video frame rather than ffmpeg process-spawn time, and startup is not declared healthy until the exact selected capture/conversion/encoder/mux graph reports a real first frame plus advancing output progress.

Every implemented GPU/encoder combination records the intended League window/region at the configured 1920x1080 and 60 FPS without game-process injection, graphics hooks inside League, input interception, anti-cheat-sensitive behavior, or automatic modification of League settings.

The optimized path preserves the existing automatic match lifecycle, fragmented-MP4 interruption tolerance, supported H.264 High recording semantics, audio-track behavior, match association, metadata, Live Client polling, graceful finalization, and recoverable partial-output behavior; source recordings are never destructively rewritten by migration or verification. Future codec/profile support requires a native implementation and the same evidence before it becomes configurable.

Loss of the capture surface, adapter reset, League window replacement, focus/visibility transitions, encoder failure, and unsupported capture capability produce deterministic lifecycle behavior and actionable diagnostics without a deadlock, runaway retry loop, resource leak, silently frozen-success state, or corrupted finalized-success claim.

No GPU vendor or encoder combination silently falls back to `gdigrab`, system-memory capture, an FFmpeg-driven WGC recorder, or another parallel capture backend. Unsupported native combinations fail with explicit diagnostics and are excluded from GPU-native, GPU-agnostic-performance, and negligible-impact claims.

A canonical support matrix distinguishes `implemented`, `automated-tested`, `hardware-validated`, `performance-validated`, `unsupported`, and `unvalidated` for Windows versions, capture capabilities, NVIDIA/NVENC, codecs, and relevant adapter combinations. Unimplemented AMD/AMF and Intel/QSV native adapters are `unsupported`; only an implemented combination awaiting available physical hardware may be `unvalidated`.

Automated tests cover the native WGC/D3D11/NVENC plan, adapter matching, integrated/discrete and cross-adapter rejection, unsupported codec/profile/vendor configuration, bounded-buffer behavior, deterministic frame-drop/backpressure accounting, resource release, capture-surface loss/recreation, encoder/mux failure, shutdown/finalization ordering, absence of cross-backend fallback, and recording metadata semantics using fakes or dedicated fixtures where real GPU behavior cannot be deterministic.

The Windows build compiles and packages the complete supported native WGC/D3D11/NVENC recorder without requiring a developer-installed capture or encoder SDK. Runtime requirements and actionable failure messages are documented; an unavailable NVENC path fails without activating a software, external-capture, or another-vendor encoder.

The capture collector/analyzer contract is versioned and records capture backend, diagnostics ABI, adapter identity, interop, runtime build, support label, and target encoder; historical schema-v1 evidence remains readable, schema-v2 requires one capped baseline/capture pair plus one uncapped baseline/capture pair, and one-recorder/one-FFmpeg-audio-mux topology plus every per-run validity/resource gate remain intact. Unsupported AMF/QSV targets are rejected until their draft native-adapter features are implemented.

A controlled Windows integration test on available hardware proves that the native backend acquires and encodes a changing 1920x1080 60-FPS fixture for at least the defined test duration, keeps buffer/resource counts bounded, reports capture and direct-NVENC paths separately, produces expected audio/video streams, and yields a file that passes ffprobe plus full ffmpeg decode.

A valid post-change Ryzen 5 5600X/RTX 4060/1920x1080 NVENC League comparison consisting of one capped baseline/capture pair and one uncapped baseline/capture pair passes every capped frame gate: average-FPS loss <=2%, 1%-low FPS loss <=5%, p95 frametime increase <=5%, p99 frametime increase <=8%, and additional dropped-frame rate <=0.1 percentage point. If the pair is noisy, contradictory, or invalid, it is replaced by a fresh complete pair rather than averaged with mandatory repetitions.

The same valid NVENC comparison passes every QB-PERF-001 resource-safety gate, shows no sustained recorder/ffmpeg memory growth, output stall, process disappearance, encoder/poller lifecycle error, media-integrity failure, CPU >=90% saturation regression, or GPU 3D >=95% saturation regression, and reduces median system/League CPU deltas below the protocol's 2-percentage-point substantial-finding threshold or records a reviewed evidence-backed disposition that does not contradict negligible game impact.

The QB-PERF-001 capped frame and resource-safety budgets are the common performance contract for every future native GPU/encoder combination before it may be declared supported. This feature validates only native NVENC; unimplemented vendors remain unsupported and are owned by draft implementation-plus-validation follow-ups, so QueueBack makes no vendor-wide negligible-impact claim.

The uncapped diagnostic pair is retained and analyzed independently. It does not gate capped completion, but every substantial uncapped frame/resource finding has a concrete canonical disposition and no result is hidden by aggregate reporting.

The finalized benchmark report records the exact native backend, capture API, copy/conversion path, physical adapter, direct NVENC boundary, codec, profile, resolution, FPS, binary/config revisions, all four individual runs, media validation, diagnostics, and remaining limitations; it validates only the available NVENC target and identifies draft native AMF/QSV follow-ups without presenting those unimplemented vendors as failed or unvalidated product paths.

Applicable recorder and project-wide verification passes on the completed tree, relevant capture architecture and operator documentation is updated, and concrete benchmark/integration evidence is recorded in this feature before it can be marked done.

features.notes: This feature owns the vendor-neutral Windows capture core, bounded GPU-resident frame path, native encoder boundary, and common performance contract. It is not a polling or NVIDIA-preset optimization. The client and recorder must retain stable release-era bundle behavior; QB-CAP-002 state/classification work remains outside scope. features.name: Replay-oriented GOP and Fragment Experiment
features.description: Compare the current two-second recording GOP/fragment baseline with one-second and 500-millisecond candidates across recorder overhead, media integrity, replay seek behavior, and keyframe-aligned export opportunities before changing production media policy.
evidence: The native recorder currently uses a 120-frame/two-second IDR cadence at 60 FPS, no B-frames, and keyframe-fragmented MP4; this is a reasonable replay baseline but has not been compared with shorter cadences in the real app.

acceptance_criteria: A test-only, identity-recorded matrix compares two seconds, one second, and 500 milliseconds on every retained recorder backend using otherwise matched codec/profile/resolution/FPS/audio/runtime settings and dedicated changing-media fixtures.

Recorder measurements include CPU/GPU, frame pacing/lateness, queue/backpressure counters, memory/handles/threads, bitrate/file size, fragment/mux cost, startup/stop/finalization, output progress, and full media/accounting integrity under the unchanged QB-PERF-002 reliability/performance contract.

Replay measurements include cold/warm opening, near/far seek p50/p95/p99, request-to-first-presented latency, keyframe-to-target decode distance, frame stepping, rapid scrub after thumbnail feedback, and current WebView resource stability.

Export measurements report the share and latency of exactly keyframe-aligned compatible ranges under the future QB-CLIP-004 decision contract without silently shifting user endpoints or implementing smart-cut/edge-only re-encoding.

Each candidate is tested with actual ffprobe packet/frame facts and full decode; backend-specific B-frame/time-base/fragment differences remain explicit and no result is inferred from configured encoder names.

Production recorder settings remain unchanged unless one candidate provides a repeatable user-visible replay/export win and passes every unchanged capture reliability, League-impact, media-integrity, size/quality, and lifecycle gate; otherwise the current two-second baseline is retained with evidence.
Timestamp-aware muxing, multiple audio stems, ReplayIndex generation on the recorder hot path, backend removal, and playback-engine replacement remain outside this experiment.

features.name: Packaged Media Tool Contract
features.description: Bundle ffmpeg and ffprobe as Windows application resources and give recorder diagnostics, capture, probing, thumbnailing, and clip export one explicit installed-tool discovery contract.
evidence: 2026-08-12 completion claim: one shared paired media-runtime contract, an embedded exact lock, finite capability validation, explicit offline source build/staging, Windows resource mapping, PATH rejection, operation-scoped app degradation, sanitized-PATH smoke, and portable release verification are implemented.

The pinned QueueBack FFmpeg 8.1.2 build passed real NVENC diagnostics on driver 566.03 after the incompatible generic build was rejected. Runtime/recorder/Tauri/frontend/release, benchmark regression, canonical-state, and diff checks passed; exact tool hashes and detailed command results are retained in the execution record.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in Windows-x86_64 media-runtime lock pins one reproducible QueueBack FFmpeg 8.1.2 build by exact FFmpeg, nv-codec-header, and AMF tags/40-character commits, exact toolchain package versions, build identity/configuration, and individual ffmpeg/ffprobe hashes. Floating latest sources, a self-asserted adjacent manifest, and executable-name-only discovery are not trusted runtime identities.

One shared Rust contract resolves ffmpeg and ffprobe as an indivisible pair from a complete media-runtime directory. On Windows, recorder and app production paths use the packaged resource root; an explicit QUEUEBACK_MEDIA_RUNTIME_DIR development override must satisfy the same lock, while PATH, LEAGUE_REPLAY_FFMPEG, mixed directories, and a partial pair cannot silently satisfy the contract.

The version-two runtime layout contains runtime-manifest.json, bin/ffmpeg.exe, bin/ffprobe.exe, applicable FFmpeg/x264/NVIDIA/AMD/Intel licenses and notices, exact source/build provenance, and no unrelated ffplay binary. Relative manifest paths are traversal-safe, every required file is a regular file inside the runtime root, and on-disk identity is checked against the lock embedded in both QueueBack binaries.

Runtime validation is finite and distinguishes missing/incomplete files, invalid manifest or path, hash/integrity mismatch, wrong architecture/version/build, ffmpeg/ffprobe pair mismatch, blocked execution, probe timeout, and missing capability. The baseline capability report proves gfxcapture, scale_d3d11, D3D11 hardware support, libx264, and compiled NVENC, AMF, and QSV H.264/HEVC encoders without misrepresenting compiled support as hardware availability or measured vendor performance.

Runtime acquisition/build is an explicit maintainer action: the checked-in script clones only the pinned tagged commits when `-Acquire` is explicitly supplied, rejects commit or toolchain-version drift, builds in the ignored workspace tree, and stages only locked files through a temporary directory. Ordinary tests, Cargo/npm builds, application startup, and recording never download, rebuild, update, or mutate the packaged runtime, and generated sources/binaries remain outside source control.

The Windows Tauri resource configuration maps the staged directory to one stable resources/media-runtime location, and the standalone recorder resolves that same location relative to its installed executable. A release-layout verifier proves the exact required file set and hashes; QB-DIST-004 remains responsible for the final installer and clean-machine upgrade/uninstall workflow.

Recorder diagnostics, encoder discovery/benchmarking, and recording child creation receive ffmpeg only from the resolved MediaTools value. The path is resolved and validated once before recording startup, is logged/reported explicitly, and adds no per-frame or periodic active-recording work.

App probing, thumbnail generation, and clip export receive ffprobe/ffmpeg only from the same resolved MediaTools value. A missing or invalid runtime does not make an otherwise valid recording Unknown or prevent library browsing/playback; only media-tool-dependent operations are unavailable and return the stable actionable runtime error.

A staged Windows release-layout check with a sanitized PATH proves recorder diagnostics plus dedicated temporary-fixture encode/probe/thumbnail/export operations use the packaged pair successfully. It does not start the legacy GDI recorder, alter a user recording, require a real League session, or stand in for QB-PERF-002's capture and performance proof.

The contract has one explicit extension point for QB-PERF-002 to apply its minimal audited capture-diagnostics patch to this same QueueBack 8.1.2 source build and require the diagnostics ABI without adding another resolver or accepting PATH fallback. Applicable shared-contract, recorder, Tauri, frontend, packaging, feature-list, and project-wide checks pass with concrete evidence before completion.
